Pramipexole is a well-established dopamine D2/D3 receptor agonist with decades of clinical use; target engagement is assumed from the mechanism and supported by the observed UPDRS improvements (motor function changes consistent with dopaminergic activity). No direct PD/PK biomarker of receptor occupancy was reported, but the clinical response pattern (previous placebo patients showing greater UPDRS improvement upon initiating PPX ER) is consistent with target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: UPDRS II+III and UPDRS III changes from open-label baseline reflect dopaminergic motor pathway modulation. Previous placebo patients showed UPDRS II+III improvement of -3.6 and UPDRS III improvement of -3.1, consistent with dopamine receptor agonism restoring motor function. Previous PPX ER patients showed smaller changes (+1.1 UPDRS II+III, +0.7 UPDRS III), consistent with already being at steady-state on the drug. This differential pattern supports pathway modulation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint was a safety endpoint (percentage of patients with AEs over 80 weeks), which was met — 83.7% AE rate, 48.8% ADR rate, 8.9% SAE rate. This is a safety/tolerability study by design, not an efficacy trial. The secondary UPDRS endpoints showed statistically significant improvements (p=0.0039 for UPDRS II+III, p=0.0015 for UPDRS III in the previous placebo subgroup), supporting clinical translation of the dopaminergic mechanism. 4. CGI-I and PGI-I responder rates were higher in previously treated groups, likely reflecting maintained benefit. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a single-arm open-label extension with no concurrent control arm, limiting causal inference for efficacy. The primary endpoint is safety-focused. The UPDRS improvements in the previous placebo group represent a treatment-initiation effect rather than long-term maintenance. Overall, the trial met its primary safety objective and showed supportive efficacy signals consistent with the known mechanism of pramipexole.
